summary: Audited paper/es-threequarter-note.tex: the ONLY ineffective input is Bombieri–Vinogradov (eq. BV, R=26) in the lower bound of Thm supply, over moduli q=4uv ∈ (4X^{1/24}, 4x^{1/3}]; BT, Shiu, lattice sums, moments, void and ledger are effective. BMOR (arXiv:1802.00085, Thm 1.1/1.2 verified: valid only for x ≥ exp(0.03√q log³q) when q>10⁵) cannot replace it — the range is never met for q ≥ X^{1/24}, and pointwise x/(φ(q)log x) bounds summed over q are structurally too weak; Platt–Trudgian is irrelevant here. Assessment (proof sketch): an effective BV off one Landau–Page modulus r1 (Akbary–Hambrook Thm 1.2, explicit c0=48.83, for conductors > (log x)^31; effective zero-free region below) plus BMOR Prop 1.11 (β ≤ 1−40/(√q log²q)) for r1 ≤ (log x)^{1.9}, and dropping the triples with r1 | 4uv (relative mass loss ≪ (log x)^{−1.9+ε}) otherwise, makes c_*, C_* of the 3/4 theorem effective. Premise of `why` fails: N·exp(−c(log N)^{3/4}) → ∞, so no effective/explicit version can ever certify 'no counterexample below X' (data/z52b/pass2/ZF1/Z2418/effectivity.md §5).
not_done: No rewrite of the note; Shiu constant not made explicit (so 'effective', not 'explicit'); log log and m/n notes only grepped, not re-derived; sketch not independently reviewed.

summary: Read SV (Acta Arith. 118 (2005), Thms 1–4, Props 2–3: limit law c_r = Haar measure of lattices with r points in Ω for UNIFORM random congruences mod p, error O(p^{−δ})). Premise: the item's 'linear congruence mod 4cd' is inverted (in all ES divisor forms the modulus is the unknown, p the residue), so I used the exact dictionary p = 4uBC−u−B ⟺ (B,u) solves y ≡ Ax (mod p), A = 4Cu−1, and compared lattice statistics: for uniform A the empirical P(λ1(L_A) ≤ r√p) matches SV/Haar 3r²/π to 3 digits (e.g. 0.0598 vs 0.0597 at r=0.25), but over all 233 996 certificates of the 7254 primes p≡1(4) in [10⁶,1.2·10⁶] P(λ1 ≤ 0.05√p) = 0.349 (Haar 0.0024), rising to 0.463 at 347 primes near 10⁸ (18 946 certificates); log_p max(B,u) is spread over (0.05, 0.6+), not concentrated at 1/2. So ES certificates sit in the cusp (measure ≍ log²p/p of A's), exactly where SV's O(p^{−δ}) law carries no information; no size-law comparison beyond this is meaningful.
evidence: BRAINSTORM/bsA_hecke_cusp_excursions.md (same B3 scale diagnosis for QNR Hecke points)
not_done: No affine (inhomogeneous ASL2) variant and no Type I analogue; no attempt to condition SV on the sparse residue set {4Cu−1}; no residue-class (mod 840) split since the cusp concentration is generic.

summary: Literature verified (arXiv:1708.02610 abstract, Tao–Teräväinen Duke 2019): odd-order log-averaged Chowla and log density 1/8 of every Liouville sign pattern of length ≤ 3 — statements about log-averages over ALL n, silent on the sparse set N_e=(p+e)/4. Computed R(p) and (λ(N_3),…,λ(N_3+7)) (N_{e+4}=N_e+1) for all 102 327 primes p≡1(4) in [10⁶,4·10⁶]; hard = bottom decile of R/log²p within each class mod 840 (and mod 3360), compared with class-matched controls (stratified χ², 200 within-class permutations). Pattern frequencies over all primes are 1/2^k to ±0.002 (k ≤ 3); hard-vs-control: k=1 χ²=0.05 (p=0.82), k=2 χ²=10.6 (p=0.01), k=3 p=0.03, k=4 p=0.29; the k=2/3 signal is a single shift λ(N_7) (z=3.2 mod 840) that drops to z=2.3 under mod-3360 stratification (Bonferroni over 8 shifts p≈0.18), and within-class corr(λ(N_3), log(R+1)) = −0.0015. The real signal is divisor-theoretic and λ-blind: N_3 prime is enriched among hard primes (11.7% vs 10.0%, z=7.0) while λ(N_3) shows z=−0.24.
not_done: Hardness measured by R(p) (the (★) c=1 Type II line), not by full f_II; no Möbius/μ² patterns; KMT sign-pattern paper not read beyond titles/abstracts (its results are again all-n averages); primes > 4·10⁶ not tested.
